name: StageBuilder Pro
description: A 2D and 3D stage plot and technical rider for bands, DJs, and production crews, with a library of more than 200 production items. Plans are free, $10 a month, or $20 a month, or $400 once. Solo founder. Launched March 2026. About 6,546 users. US.

mentions.evidence: MRR $1,398. 177 subscriptions. Last 30 days $2,043. All-time $13,696, in about 8 months. The last 30 days are above the subscription line. There is also a $400 lifetime plan. Revenue synced 2 November 2026 ~06:58 Warsaw.
mentions.indieAngle: One document a trade has to hand over before the job.

whyItPrints: A gigging act needs a stage plot and an input list. A lot of them still draw it in a document.
whyThisMatters:
StageBuilder Pro draws the stage and writes the technical rider. Bands, DJs, and the crew. Two dimensions or three, and a library of more than two hundred items you would actually put on a stage. Free, ten a month, twenty a month, or four hundred once. One founder. It launched in March 2026. He says about sixty-five hundred users. US.

Stripe shows a bit under two hundred subscriptions. The monthly subscription line is under the last thirty days of cash. A lifetime plan is on the site, which is a plausible reason, and the listing does not itemise the invoices. Eight months of history is the all-time total. The user count is far above the paying subscriptions, so most people are on the free plan.

You pay so the venue gets a plot and an input list, instead of a drawing in a word processor.

An input list is the other document a venue demands before load-in. DJs sit alongside bands as buyers.
